subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the area of the triangle formed by the straight line x cos α + y sin α = p with the coordinate axes.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 5, book p.140. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives the first mark for the two intercepts p sec α and p cosec α, and the second for the area and the double-angle simplification. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Answer checked by a second route: writing the line as x cos α + y sin α − p = 0 and applying Δ = c²/(2|ab|) gives p²/(2|sin α cos α|) = p²/|sin 2α|, which matches the intercept route used here. LINES EXPANDED 2026-09-14 (founder direction, modelled on the Maths-2A, Maths-2B and Maths-1A expansions): every move is written on its own line, with the reason or the arithmetic shown before it is used; the steps, marks and split are unchanged.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say how you get each intercept, and which identity turns the answer into sin 2α.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the two intercepts
steps.margin_note: First mark. Put y = 0 for the x-intercept and x = 0 for the y-intercept. The line must cut both axes, so cos α and sin α are both non-zero here.
steps.memory_tip: Put y = 0 to get the x-intercept and x = 0 to get the y-intercept. That order never changes.
lines: Given line is x cos α + y sin α = p
(p ≠ 0 as well, or the line passes through the origin
Here cos α ≠ 0 and sin α ≠ 0,
else the line misses one axis.
Put y = 0:  x cos α = p  ⇒  x = p sec α
Put x = 0:  y sin α = p  ⇒  y = p cosec α

recall.must_convey: That putting y = 0 gives the x-intercept p sec α and putting x = 0 gives the y-intercept p cosec α.
accept: put y equals zero to get p sec alpha
put x equals zero to get p cosec alpha
the intercepts are p by cos alpha and p by sin alpha
y zero pettina x intercept vasthundi

steps.why: The triangle has its right angle at the origin, and its two perpendicular sides are exactly these two intercepts, so finding them is the set-up.
common_mistakes: Writing the x-intercept as p cos α instead of p/cos α.

steps.label: Compute the area
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Half the product of the intercepts, in modulus, then use 2 sin α cos α = sin 2α.
steps.memory_tip: 2 sin α cos α = sin 2α. The 2 in that identity cancels the 2 from the one half.

lines.text: (the triangle has its right angle at the origin,
and its two legs are the intercepts)
(put the intercepts p sec α and p cosec α)
(2|sin α cos α| = |2 sin α cos α|)

recall.must_convey: That the area is half the product of the intercepts in modulus, and equals p² divided by the modulus of sin 2α.
accept: half into the product of the two intercepts
p squared by two sin alpha cos alpha
two sin alpha cos alpha is sin two alpha
the area is p squared by mod sin two alpha

steps.why: The modulus is needed because sec α and cosec α change sign with the quadrant of α, while an area is always positive.
common_mistakes: Dropping the modulus and reporting a negative area for an obtuse α.
Writing sin 2α as 2 sin α and losing the cos α.
